differentiators.sectionTitle: Three things other chat tools don't do
differentiators.sectionSubtitle: Sukhan was built for a market most chat tools ignore. Here's what that means in practice.

transparent.title: Transparent AI pricing
transparent.body: No metered AI charges. No per-resolution fees. Every plan has a fixed monthly AI action quota — when you hit the cap, the AI gracefully steps aside and your human agents take over. You'll never get a surprise bill.

selfHost.title: Actually self-hostable
selfHost.body: One docker compose up command. AGPL-3.0 means you can run Sukhan on your own server, for your own customers, with no license fee. The full source is yours to inspect, modify, and audit.

bilingual.title: Bilingual from day one
bilingual.body: Persian RTL isn't bolted on — it's a first-class locale. The agent dashboard, the widget, the AI prompts, and the emails all switch between Persian and English without reloading. Your visitors see what they expect to see.

ctaStrip.title: From signup to a live widget in under five minutes.
ctaStrip.body: Create a workspace, paste one script tag, start chatting. Free forever for small teams.

features.title: Built for the conversations that actually happen.
features.subtitle: Every feature here exists because a real customer-support team asked for it. No filler.

realtime.title: Real-time chat
realtime.body: Sub-second message delivery over a Socket.IO transport. Typing indicators, read receipts, presence, file attachments. The inbox handles hundreds of concurrent conversations without breaking a sweat.

faq.title: AI FAQ auto-responder
faq.body: Drop in the questions your visitors actually ask. Our LLM classifier matches new questions against your FAQ list above a confidence threshold — when it's sure, it answers; when it isn't, it stays quiet and routes to a human.

productQa.title: Product Q&A
productQa.body: Sync your product catalog from WooCommerce (Shopify + Basalam coming soon) or import a CSV. The AI answers product questions using only your data — no hallucination, no invented prices.

routing.title: Routing rules
routing.body: Send conversations to the right agent automatically. Route by keyword, by department, by visitor language, or by time of day. Rules are evaluated in order, the first match wins, and you can reorder them by drag-and-drop.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.body: See your volume, response times, and CSAT trends at a glance. Filter by department or agent. Export to CSV. No dashboards-of-dashboards — just the numbers that matter.

csat.title: CSAT surveys
csat.body: After every conversation, the widget asks the visitor one question: how did we do? The score lands in analytics within seconds. Set the survey text per-language.

widget.title: Widget customization
widget.body: Your widget, your brand. Pick the accent color, the launcher shape (tab / rounded / pill), the position (bottom-start or bottom-end), the agent avatar, the logo, and the greeting — separately for Persian and English.

billing.title: Iran-first billing
billing.body: Pay in Toman via ZarinPal, IDPay, or ZarinLink. No Stripe, no foreign currency, no SWIFT. Plans are flat-rate — if you hit a cap, the feature gracefully degrades instead of charging you more.

doc.title: Embed the Sukhan widget in five minutes.
doc.subtitle: Two paths to a live widget: install the NPM package for a React/Next.js app, or paste a single script tag for plain HTML. Pick the one that fits your stack.

quickStart.title: Quick start
quickStart.subtitle: Three steps from zero to a live chat widget on your page.

steps.title: Install
steps.body: Add the sukhan-widget package to your project. Works with npm, yarn, pnpm, or bun.

steps.title: Set the env var
steps.body: Add your API key to .env.local. Find it in the Sukhan dashboard → Widget → Embed.

steps.title: Import + render
steps.body: Call initSukhan() in a client-side useEffect. The widget auto-mounts the launcher button.

react.title: React / Next.js integration
react.subtitle: The widget is SSR-safe: importing it in a Next.js server component is a no-op. Initialize it inside a useEffect in a client component.
react.codeNote: Expose the API key to the client by prefixing it with NEXT_PUBLIC_ in your .env.local — Next.js inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars into the client bundle at build time.

scriptTag.title: HTML / script-tag method
scriptTag.subtitle: For non-React sites (plain HTML, WordPress, custom CMS). No build step, no bundler, no NPM. The script reads data-api-key at runtime.
scriptTag.codeTitle: Paste this once before the closing body tag
scriptTag.codeNote: The src URL is the Sukhan backend origin. If you self-host, replace with your own backend URL.

config.title: Configuration
config.subtitle: initSukhan(options) accepts the following. All keys are optional except apiKey.
config.freeNote: Free plan is LOCKED. The widget renders a small Powered-by-Sukhan badge and the launcher uses the neutral ink color. Upgrade to Pro / Business / Enterprise to remove the badge and apply your accent color across the launcher + header.

rows.description: The tenant API key (workspace slug, optionally sk_-prefixed). Falls back to process.env.SUKHAN_API_KEY then window.SUKHAN_API_KEY.
Sukhan backend base URL. Defaults to the page origin (same-domain embedding) or https://app.sukhan.chat (cross-origin NPM embedding).
Where to mount the widget. Defaults to document.body.
Force a UI locale. Defaults to the tenant defaultLocale.
Force a text direction. Defaults to the tenant defaultDirection.
Pre-identify the visitor with a name, email, or custom visitor ID.

api.title: API reference
api.subtitle: The widget talks to four public REST endpoints + one Socket.IO transport. All are CORS-enabled and rate-limited.
api.endpointsSubtitle: All under /api/widget/[slug]/. The [slug] part is your workspace slug (= API key).

endpoints.description: Fetch the widget configuration (accent, shape, position, greeting, locale, direction).
Identify the visitor. Body fields: visitorId, email?, name?. Returns: contactId, conversationId, realtimeToken.
Load the visitor conversation history. Query: ?conversationId=...
Send a visitor message. Body field: text. Returns: message, conversationId.
Submit a CSAT rating. Body fields: conversationId, rating (1-5), comment?.

api.socketSubtitle: Socket.IO connection over the Caddy gateway. The realtime token (from POST /contact) is passed in the auth field.
api.authBody: The visitor realtime token is a short-lived JWT signed with the backend NEXTAUTH_SECRET. It encodes the visitor type, contact ID, tenant ID, and slug. Sent as Authorization Bearer token on REST requests and as auth token on the Socket.IO handshake.
api.rateBody: 30 req/min per IP address. 60 req/min per tenant (slug). 429 responses include a Retry-After header. Dev mode skips rate limiting for localhost.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.subtitle: Common issues and how to fix them.

items.q: The widget doesn't appear on my page
items.a: Check the browser console for [sukhan] errors. The most common is a missing API key. Verify SUKHAN_API_KEY (or NEXT_PUBLIC_SUKHAN_API_KEY for Next.js) is set AND exposed to the client. Confirm the backend is reachable: curl /api/widget/[your-slug]/config should return JSON, not a 404.

items.q: Real-time messages arrive after a 10-second delay
items.a: The 10s delay means the polling fallback is delivering the message instead of Socket.IO. Causes: (1) NEXTAUTH_SECRET mismatch between the Next.js app and the realtime service — both processes must use the same secret. (2) The reverse proxy is stripping the XTransformPort query param or the WebSocket upgrade headers. (3) An ad blocker is blocking /socket.io.min.js — the polling fallback handles this gracefully.

items.q: I am on the free plan and the widget shows a Powered-by-Sukhan badge
items.a: That is expected behavior. Free-plan widgets are LOCKED: the launcher uses the neutral ink color and the panel shows a small Powered-by-Sukhan footer. Upgrade to Pro / Business / Enterprise to remove the badge and apply your own accent color.

The widget looks for the API key in three places, in priority order: (1) options.apiKey passed to initSukhan, (2) window.SUKHAN_API_KEY (runtime injection), (3) process.env.SUKHAN_API_KEY (build-time replacement). If none are set, init throws. Set at least one.

items.q: Cross-origin embedding fails with CORS errors
items.a: All public widget endpoints set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so CORS shouldn't be an issue. If you see CORS errors, you may be hitting a dashboard endpoint (which is same-origin only) — the widget endpoints are all under /api/widget/[slug]/. Or your reverse proxy may be stripping the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.

items.q: How do I force a specific locale?
items.a: Pass locale: en (or fa) to initSukhan(). Without an override, the widget uses the tenant defaultLocale from the dashboard.
